text:
incident-bot: ALERT: high latency detected for customer Silverfin (dedicated pool eu1). p95=420ms -> 1200ms, p99=2.1s. Error rate steady. 18% of tenant requests above p99 threshold. Route: /v1/generate (redwood-large-v2).
ben: I'm on call — joining warroom. pulling metrics now.
jamie: I see correlated queue depth spike on pool-sf-eu1-dedicated-3, KV cache miss rate up ~30%.
maya: adding context: autocast quantized instances report increased GC-like pauses on 32-bit host. could be kernel scheduling under high batch pressure.
leo: can we isolate Silverfin tenant to a spare pool? warm spare available: pool-sf-eu1-warm-1 with capacity for 120 RPS.
ben: ok plan: 1) throttle non-critical routes for Silverfin (rerank/analytics) 2) move /v1/generate traffic to warm spare via routing policy 3) scale dedicated pool by +2 GPUs, start eviction if needed.
alexa: CSM: informing customer in 15m. message: "We're seeing increased latency in eu1 for some requests; working on mitigation now. We'll update in 30m."
kyra: pinging infra to prewarm GPUs for scaling: @infra please confirm boot ETA.
jamie: infra response (internal): "prewarm request submitted — ~8 min to ready on eu1 zone B."
maya: quick mitigation suggestion: enable aggressive prefix/KV caching for Silverfin for 30m window. reduces compute per-request.
ben: doing cache enable now: command pasted: ```/api/admin/cache/enable?tenant=silverfin&mode=prefix&ttl=300```
leo: routing change ready — will cut 40% of production generate traffic to pool-sf-eu1-warm-1 as canary.
jamie: logs snippet from pool-sf-eu1-dedicated-3: ```WARN  [2025-11-02T14:12:03Z] queue_wait_ms=450 batch_size=64 kv_miss=1```
maya: that batch_size spikes to 128 during peak; kernel scheduler hitting context switch cost. applying temporary limiter: max_batch_size=64 for redwood-large-v2 on pool-sf-eu1-dedicated-3.
ben: limiter applied. watching metrics.
(alexa reacts with :eyes:)
ben: initial canary routing to warm spare shows p95 down to 310ms for routed subset. p99 for remainder still at ~1.9s.
leo: start scale +2 GPUs now; ETA 9m. also spinning up an alternative model variant redwood-large-v2-quant to accept overflow if needed.
jamie: if latency doesn't drop after routing+cache+limiter, plan B: isolate tenant (eviction) and move remaining traffic to dedicated spare or fallback model entirely. Eviction is last resort — impacts throughput.
alexa: customer reply (via CSM): "Thanks — please prioritize eu1. We're seeing production errors on a small % of sessions, but can accept brief degraded throughput while local issues fixed."
ben: noted. keep CSM updated every 15m.
kyra: infra confirms +2 GPUs live in 7m.
maya: after limiter + canary + cache, p95 for Silverfin overall dropped to 360ms, p99 to 1.1s. error rate unchanged. good progress.
ben: continuing monitoring. create incident ticket and assign postmortem to eng-runtime. I'll hand off in 40m to night oncall.
jamie: recording actions for postmortem: "root cause likely batch pressure + KV cache miss leading to higher scheduling pauses on dedicated hosts. mitigations: routing to warm spare, reduce max_batch_size, enable prefix cache, scale GPUs, prepare fallback quantized model."
leo: I'll file infra follow-up: investigate host scheduling/CPU steal metrics and kernel tunables for our instance class.
alexa: drafted customer update ready to send after next checkpoint.
ben: checkpoint in 15. if stable, we'll transition to containment and close warroom. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity reduced to SEV-2. Mitigations in place. Next update at +15m.
